::: {.callout-note}
**This page is for the facilitator.** It is rendered with the site but left out of the navbar, so nothing on the site links to it. The track pages under `tracks/` are participant-facing and contain no instructor guidance, which is collected here together with the notes on the variant decks. The [facilitator guide of the EU-frames case](eu-frames-guide.qmd) is the run sheet for its one-day replication format, the [facilitator guide of the housing-audit case](housing-guide.qmd) the run sheet for both formats of that case, the [facilitator guide of the immigration-and-trust case](trust-guide.qmd) the run sheet for its one-day format, and the [facilitator guide of the cohabitation case](cohabitation-guide.qmd) the run sheet for its one-day format.
:::

## The six formats of the EU-frames case

Every format is an ordered route through pages that already exist on the site, with a docked sidebar of its own (`_sidebar.yml`) and a slides page embedding the deck it runs on. The decks are assembled from one pool of slides: `slides/eu-frames-full.qmd` is the full deck, and the variants under `slides/` include the same segment files (`slides/_segments/eu-frames/`) in a different order, with their own agenda, aims and part-divider slides.

| Format | Pages | Deck | Optional runs in the main flow |
|---|---|---|---|
| One day – open science and replication | `tracks/eu-frames-one-day-replication/` | `slides/eu-frames-one-day-replication.qmd`, the delivered deck as it stands | none; all four runs are switched by the `d` key |
| One day – social data science tools | `tracks/eu-frames-one-day-tools/` | `slides/eu-frames-one-day-tools.qmd` | the tools slides and the R tutorial |
| One day – an introduction to the statistical methods | `tracks/eu-frames-one-day-methods/` | `slides/eu-frames-one-day-methods.qmd` | the methodological tutorial and the multiverse tutorial |
| Three days | `tracks/eu-frames-three-days/` | `slides/eu-frames-three-days.qmd`, three day dividers, the workshop on day 2 in three parts | all four |
| Semester | `tracks/eu-frames-semester/` | `slides/eu-frames-full.qmd`, the full deck | all four |
| Self-study | `tracks/eu-frames-self-study/` | `slides/eu-frames-full.qmd`, the full deck | all four |

**How the runs are switched.** In the segment files, every slide of an optional run is marked with `.deepdive` and a `run` attribute: `tools` (five slides in the Part 1 tools segment), `r` (the ten-slide R tutorial), `methods` (the twelve-slide methodological tutorial) and `multiverse` (the eight-slide multiverse tutorial). A deck lists the runs that belong to its main flow under `core-runs:` in its YAML, and `slides/core-runs.lua` strips the `.deepdive` mark from those headings, so `nav-tools.html` neither hides them on the `d` key nor badges them as optional. A run that is not listed stays optional: it is hidden in lean mode and has the escape-hatch link on its first slide.

**Why no segment is included twice in one deck.** The segment files contain R chunks with labels, and knitr refuses a duplicate label, so each deck includes each segment at most once. That is why day 2 of the three-day deck has no methodological or multiverse tutorial: both move to day 3, where they are core. It is also why the two focused one-day decks each leave whole segments out rather than repeating a slide in two places.

**Pages that every format shares.** Every format starts from the [case study](../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd), which tells the original study, SCORE and Multi100, the five reanalysts with an assessment of their choices, and the conversion lesson on how Multi100 turned their statistics into one effect size; each track index links it first. The specification menu is taught as the full set of fourteen decisions, on the [decision map](../cases/eu-frames/map.qmd) and the [specification menu](../cases/eu-frames/menu.qmd), with the curve of 864 specifications as the subset that an audit judged justifiable for this claim. The helpers of the browser lab and of the workspace refuse an option that is off the curve, with the one-sentence reason recorded in `data/menu_options.csv` and the page that teaches the option, so a participant who asks for pooled OLS or a population weight is sent to the right page instead of being given a number. Every result is classed by the wild cluster bootstrap by country; the reproduced specification (t = −3.804, r = −0.242) has a bootstrap p of 0.110 and is not significant under that rule, which is worth saying before anyone asks.

**Rebuilding a deck.** Edit the segment files for content, or the variant `.qmd` for order and framing, and render the deck on its own: `quarto render slides/eu-frames-one-day-tools.qmd`. The project render fails at its final move step on this machine, so decks are rendered one at a time.

## The one-day replication format

The [facilitator guide](eu-frames-guide.qmd) is the run sheet for this format, and its compression ladder and never-cut list are there. Take time from a tutorial before you take it from a task, because each following part builds on what the tasks produced. Seven things stay in whatever else goes: the five-analyst forest with its software column, the estimand exercise in Part 2, the half-built graph and its adjustment set, the reproduction and the waterfall of t values that follows it, the Task 4 submission, the preregistration moment in Part 4, and the reveal of which fork accounts for the largest share of the variation.

A two-minute stretch sits between the five-analyst forest and the tools segment in Part 1, and another between the estimands run and the graphs in Part 2; neither is on the participant pages.

## The tools-focused day

The deck reorders the pool so that the toolchain gets Part 2 to itself and the R tutorial runs inside the day. What has moved, and what it costs:

- **Part 1** contains the credibility talk, SCORE, Multi100 and the open-source slide, then the pair of slides on the workspace and on what the tools cannot do, and Task 1. It is ten minutes lighter on talk than the replication day, and the setup task still runs into the break.
- **Part 2** is the tools segment in full (all five optional slides in the main flow) followed by the ten-slide R tutorial, worked live in the workspace. The tutorial is the compressible part if Part 1 overran; the plain-text and render-pipeline slides are not.
- **Part 3** is the paper, Lundberg's three steps, the DAG crash course and our own claim, then Task 2, the constrained-task slides and the Task 3 reproduction. The estimands run (the red-card strip, the four football estimands, the collapse of the spread) is not in this deck, and the DAG course should drop to confounder, mediator and paths if the reproduction is at risk. The reproduction waterfall stays.
- **Part 4** is the menu, Task 4, the class-chart debrief, the critics and what preregistration settles, then the archiving segment (the three OSF addresses, the Multi100 preregistration, the preregistration templates and the eight AsPredicted questions) before the declaration. The fork-importance reveal, the percentile beat and the inference literacy segment are not in this deck; if the class wants them, `g` jumps to any slide in the full deck.

The joining instructions for this format should ask people to do section 6 of the IDE module before the day, so that Part 2 is spent on what the tools are for rather than on whether they start.

## The methods-focused day

The deck keeps the DAG crash course, the methodological tutorial and the multiverse tutorial in the main flow and drops the tools segment, SCORE and the archiving segment.

- **Part 1** is the credibility talk, the vocabulary slides (the matrix, repeatability and credibility, the quick-check pair, open research), Multi100 from the inside and the pair of slides on the workspace and on what the tools cannot do, then Task 1. The three SCORE studies are not in this deck. The five-analyst forest still is, and it still sets up the day.
- **Part 2** runs the paper, the estimands run, Lundberg, the DAG course in full and our own claim, with the R tutorial left optional. If the class is behind at the graph, take time from the Model 1 and Model 2 slide, not from the estimand waterfall.
- **Part 3** is the constrained task, the reproduction, the menu and the methodological tutorial in full, then Task 4. The tutorial is the point of the day; the compressible slides are the copredictor and weights slides.
- **Part 4** opens with the multiverse tutorial in full, then the class chart, the bet and the fork-importance reveal, the percentile, the inference literacy segment with its discussion beat, the critics and preregistration, and the declaration. The archiving segment is not in this deck, so the mapping table for the AsPredicted questions is not on screen: put the [preregistration section of the specification menu](../cases/eu-frames/menu.qmd) in the chat before Task 5.

The joining instructions for this format should ask people to read sections 1 to 3 of the statistical-methods module and fit one model before the day.

## Three days

Day 1 is the part that compresses. A cohort that already writes R and renders documents keeps the setup check and the toolchain talk and runs the course over two days; a cohort that writes R but has never met Quarto keeps session 4 alone. Day 3 compresses by moving reading out of class time rather than by cutting topics: the later sections of the statistical-methods module, from the weights section onward, work well as reading between sessions.

Day 2 does not compress. It is the one-day replication format minus what day 1 covered, and its never-cut list holds in full. In the three-day deck the workshop runs as three parts across the four sessions: the claim and its estimand across sessions 1 and 2, reproduction and exploration in session 3, multiverse and preregistration in session 4, with the tutorials moved to day 3.

A group whose data are individual respondents can put [The individual level](../companion/individual-level.qmd) in place of the simulation half of session 4 on day 3. A group that will publish code together should give the git module a session of its own rather than the half-hour it shares with the repositories module.

## Semester

**What a participant has built.** By session 10 each person holds one rendered report containing a stated estimand and its causal graph, a reproduction of a published result, a preregistration written before the analysis ran, a declared specification with its two-sentence justification, and the result that came back, all of it in a repository that another person can clone and re-render. That artefact is the natural thing for a course to be assessed on; how it is weighted, marked or moderated is a matter for the programme that runs the track.

**What compresses.** Sessions 6 and 7 cover the extension material, so a nine-week term drops one of them and folds the null-world section of the simulation module into session 10. Session 4 can be trimmed to sections 1 to 3 of the statistical-methods module, with fixed and random effects met on the workshop day instead. Sections 6 to 9 of that module are optional depth for the term rather than part of any session. Session 10 has the most material of any session that is not the workshop day, so the conversion lesson in section 4 of the case study is the natural piece to set as reading before it meets. Session 3 shortens for a group that already writes Quarto, and session 2 for a group that already writes R, but do not drop both: the grammar-of-graphics part of the R module is what makes the class chart readable in session 9.

**What must not be cut.** The reproduction in Task 3 and the declaration in Task 5 are the two ends of the whole exercise. The estimand and the graph in session 5 are what stop the specification menu reading as a list of arbitrary switches. And the preregistration has to be written before the analysis runs, in session 8 or on the day itself.

**The deck on the day.** Session 9 runs on the full deck. Press `d` at the start to switch the optional runs off, then switch the multiverse tutorial back on when Part 4 reaches it (the escape-hatch link on its first slide, or `d` again), because the module behind it is session 10.

## Self-study

The self-study pages contain their own compression notes, written to the participant, because no facilitator is there to apply them. What the facilitator can still do for a self-study cohort is keep the live results pipeline running between deliveries, so that a dot submitted alone appears on the Multiverse page and the archived cohorts stay visible beside it (`facilitator/live-results-setup.md`).

## The two formats of the housing-audit case

The housing-audit case has two tracks, because its statistics are simple enough that the tools, methods and open-research days of the EU-frames case collapse into one day. The decks include the case-neutral segments of `slides/_segments/shared/` and the segments of the case in `slides/_segments/housing/`; the setup chunk of the case comes after the shared one and gives the shared segments the addresses of the case.

| Format | Pages | Deck | Optional runs in the main flow |
|---|---|---|---|
| Short session, two to three hours | `tracks/housing-short/` | `slides/housing-short.qmd` | none; the multiverse background of the second half is on the `d` key |
| One day | `tracks/housing-one-day/` | `slides/housing-one-day.qmd` | none; the tour of the toolchain and of R in the morning and the closer look at the statistics in the afternoon are on the `d` key, so that a facilitator can lean the day towards tools or towards methods |

The [run sheet of the case](housing-guide.qmd) has the timings of both formats, the expected numbers, the checks before the day and the order of what to cut. The short session leaves the preregistration of Task 5 for afterwards; the one-day track keeps it in Part 4, beside the replication with new data.

## The one-day format of the immigration-and-trust case

The immigration-and-trust case has one track, a day of four parts of ninety minutes (`tracks/trust-one-day/`), on the deck `slides/trust-one-day.qmd`. Like the housing-audit decks, it includes the case-neutral segments of `slides/_segments/shared/` and the segments of the case in `slides/_segments/trust/`, whose setup chunk comes after the shared one.

| Format | Pages | Deck | Optional runs in the main flow |
|---|---|---|---|
| One day | `tracks/trust-one-day/` | `slides/trust-one-day.qmd` | none; the tools slides of Part 1 and the R tutorial of Part 2 (the `tools` run) and the methods tutorial of Part 3 and the multiverse background of Part 4 (the `methods` run) are on the `d` key |

The case asks more of a class than the housing-audit case and less than the EU-frames case. Its data are about 120,000 respondents in one file that ships with the workspace, so no participant downloads survey files, but every specification is a regression with controls and fixed effects, and the errors rest on 16 countries. A class that has met regression before can take the methods run in Part 3; a class of novices is better served by leaving it off and giving the time to Task 4. The [run sheet of the case](trust-guide.qmd) has the timings, the held answers, the expected numbers, the checks before the day and the order of what to cut.

## The one-day format of the cohabitation case

The cohabitation case has one track, a day of four parts of ninety minutes (`tracks/cohabitation-one-day/`), on the deck `slides/cohabitation-one-day.qmd`, which includes the case-neutral segments of `slides/_segments/shared/` and the segments of the case in `slides/_segments/cohabitation/`.

| Format | Pages | Deck | Optional runs in the main flow |
|---|---|---|---|
| One day | `tracks/cohabitation-one-day/` | `slides/cohabitation-one-day.qmd` | none; the tools slides of Part 1 and the R tutorial of Part 2 (the `tools` run) and the tutorial on person-period data and discrete-time models in Part 3 and the multiverse background of Part 4 (the `methods` run) are on the `d` key |

The day is built around a discovery that the class makes in Task 3: the file that Multi100 gave the analysts, from which the class reproduces the recorded test, holds almost none of the marriages of 1995. The track protects it. Before the day, participants read only sections 1 and 2 of the case study and the claim of the exercise overview; Part 2 shows that the analysts split without saying why; and Task 3 adds a fifth held answer, the count of the 1995 unions and marriages in the file, which the class sends before the slide that sets the file beside the rebuild appears. The workspace report explains the finding just below the chunk that makes the count, so ask the class not to read ahead. The statistics are the hardest of the three smaller cases, because every specification is a multinomial model on person-months, so a class of novices is better served by leaving the `methods` run off and walking the life table slowly. The [run sheet of the case](cohabitation-guide.qmd) has the timings, the held answers, the expected numbers, the checks before the day and the order of what to cut.

## The semester across the four cases

The semester track (`tracks/semester/`) takes the exercise through the four cases in the order of the ladder, twelve weekly sessions for a class that meets for about two hours and works three to four hours more alone. Weeks 1 and 2 set up the tools on the housing-audit data, weeks 3 and 4 run the housing-audit case, weeks 5 to 7 the immigration-and-trust case, weeks 8 and 9 the cohabitation case, weeks 10 and 11 the EU-frames case, and week 12 is the final project. The week pages put the slides and most of the tasks in the class meeting and the papers, the case studies and the modules between meetings. The run sheets of the four cases, for the [housing-audit case](housing-guide.qmd), the [immigration-and-trust case](trust-guide.qmd), the [cohabitation case](cohabitation-guide.qmd) and the [EU-frames case](eu-frames-guide.qmd), hold the expected numbers, the held answers and the fallbacks that the class meetings need.

**What a student builds.** Four case reports, one rendered workspace report for each case, each with the estimand statement and the graph, the reproduction of Task 3, the exploration of Task 4, a preregistration completed before its specification ran, and the result with its place on the curve. Then a final project that goes beyond the claim of one case, preregistered before week 12 and run in it, with the four reports and the project in one git repository whose first commit for the project is its preregistration as handed in. The licensed Eurobarometer files and the respondent file built from them stay out of that repository. Those five pieces are the natural things to assess; how they are weighted, marked or moderated is a matter for the programme that runs the track.

**The decks, week by week.** The term uses the one-day deck of each case, opened by each week page at the part that it needs.

| Weeks | Deck | Parts |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `slides/housing-one-day.qmd` | Part 1: the credibility talk, SCORE and Multi100, the tools segment and Task 1 |
| 3 and 4 | `slides/housing-one-day.qmd` | Part 2 and the reproduction of Part 3 in week 3; the menu, the methods and Part 4 in week 4 |
| 5 to 7 | `slides/trust-one-day.qmd` | Part 2 in week 5, Part 3 to the menu in week 6, the menu and Part 4 in week 7 |
| 8 and 9 | `slides/cohabitation-one-day.qmd` | Part 2 in week 8, Parts 3 and 4 in week 9 |
| 10 and 11 | `slides/eu-frames-full.qmd`, the full deck | Parts 2 and 3 to the reproduction in week 10, the menu and Part 4 in week 11 |

From week 5 on, every deck repeats the case-neutral segments that the class met on the housing-audit case: Part 1, the estimands run, the causal-graph crash course, the critics of the multiverse and the slides on the archive. Jump past them with `g`. In the decks of the immigration-and-trust and cohabitation cases, switch the optional runs off with `d` at the start of each meeting, so that the tools slides and the R tutorial stay hidden, and bring the `methods` run back when Part 3 reaches it in weeks 6 and 9, by the link on its first slide or by `d` again, because those weeks teach what it shows. The full deck of the EU-frames case carries every run in its main flow, so in weeks 10 and 11 pass over its R tutorial with `g` and keep the methodological and multiverse tutorials.

**The class charts.** Each case has a chart of its own on its Multiverse page, and each chart reads only the rows of its own case from the shared results Form. The labels of the housing-audit, immigration-and-trust and cohabitation cases carry the case word after the tag (`explore: [amber-otter-42] housing …`), while those of the EU-frames case keep the frozen format without one. Each workspace keeps its own tag in `.class-tag`, so ask the class to choose one nickname in week 4 and to pass it as `nickname = "..."` in every case, which lets each student, and you, find the same person on all four charts. A chart keeps the rows of earlier deliveries until the sheet is cleared, so decide before week 4 whether the cohort should see them.

**What compresses.** A ten- or eleven-week term merges weeks, and three merges work. Weeks 1 and 2 become one week for a class that already writes R and has rendered a Quarto document: keep Part 1 and the setup, and set the R and Quarto modules as reading. Weeks 3 and 4 become one long session, since the housing-audit case runs as a whole in the one-day track and its menu has only 64 specifications, with the modules of both weeks set as reading around it. Weeks 6 and 7 become one week for a class that has met multilevel models, with sections 3 to 6 of the statistical-methods module set as reading. Weeks 10 and 11 do not merge, because the download from GESIS, the rebuild of the panel and the curve of 864 each need a week of work. An eleven-week term merges weeks 3 and 4; a ten-week term merges weeks 1 and 2 as well.

**What must not be cut.** The four reproductions, because each teaches what the later tasks of its case build on: the continuity correction, the file of the analysts and its vote controls, the file whose 1995 rows the class inspects, and the panel with its conventional errors. Every preregistration completed and rendered before its specification runs, the final project included, whose preregistration is due before week 12 meets. And the discovery in the cohabitation case. In week 8 the track links only sections 1 and 2 of the case study, the claim on the exercise overview, Tasks 1 and 2 of the lab, the codebook of the union file and sections 1 and 2 of the event-history module. The later sections of the case study, the menu, the decision map, the multiverse page, the cheatsheet, the codebook of the SCORE file, and section 3 of the event-history module, whose last paragraph tells the story, all wait until Task 3 has been done in week 9. Keep any link that you add in week 8 inside that list.
